content: Ligand 1 is a methoxyphenyl oxadiazole amide with SA 2.37 and no activity; ligand 2 is a trifluoromethylpyridine benzamide, also dead. Neither is worth crossing. Atom 0 on ligand 1 is the methoxy methyl over an acyclic bond, the anchor that lets me discard all 25 remaining atoms and rebuild. Two runs have now plateaued at jnk3 0.50-0.52 on 2-anilinopyridines, so the question for this run is whether the pyridine ring itself is the ceiling. Everything I know says the requirement is an aryl-N(H)-azine linkage with a ring nitrogen ortho to a free donor - it does not say that nitrogen has to be pyridine's. Pyridazine is the cleanest test: it keeps the ortho nitrogen exactly where pyridine has it and adds a second nitrogen immediately beside it, raising the acceptor density at the hinge without changing the geometry or the molecule's size. I place the surviving methyl at the ring position matching pyridine's productive C4 - para to the ortho nitrogen, meta to the N-H - and keep the meta anilide and cyclobutyl cap. Expected product: about 282 Da.
